newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm olein lower ahead general election.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm olein lower ahead general election.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices edged down in early trading on Wednesday, with players staying sidelined on the eve of the general election, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,400-05 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, down from 1,405-10 rupiah at Tuesday's close. A 1,000-tonne crude palm oil tender was scheduled for later on Wednesday in the North Sumatran capital of Medan.

"Buyers are generally cautious ahead of tomorrow's elections," one trader said. "They do not want to take positions and are keeping stock levels low because they do not want to take any risks in case of any violence."

Some 125 million Indonesians are eligible to vote in the election, which has been marred by the worst political violence in the three decades of President Suharto's rule. On Wednesday morning, the Japanese embassy in Jakarta was evacuated after receiving a telephoned bomb threat from an anonymous caller.
The traders said many players would be closed for business on Thursday, while those who are open would not be delivering oil to their customers.
"Many will be closed tomorrow," one trader said. "I will be open for business but will not be delivering oil because it could be risky. I have informed my clients of this."
The traders said they expected the market, which has been subdued during most of the 27-day campaign period that ended last Friday, to return to normal in early June.
"It will take at least a week after the election for things to return to normal," one trader said.
